# v0.26.2 — long pastes reach the agent (#1016)

Qualified at the release candidate tag `v0.26.2-rc2` (`38be1f6c`): this GA tree is that tree plus this file
(RELEASE-READINESS-V1; `git diff --name-status v0.26.2-rc2..v0.26.2` = only this file).

**GA acceptance:**
- **RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet at the rc2 tag: PASS.**
  - Phase A: 15 tools; 30 matrix rows and 4 batteries, identical to `v0.26.1-rc1`'s receipt.
  - Phase B, seam check: on a live host at the tag, a 14,999-character user turn is stored as full text
    and found by full-text search; a 149,999-character user turn is stored as a stub with a preview and a
    read hint; tool output behaves as in `v0.26.1`. 4 of 4 checks pass.
  - Phase B, adversarial sweep of `v0.26.1..v0.26.2-rc2` (six dimensions, upgrade/migration included, six finders
    across two model families): 0 P0/P1 findings, so no verification was needed; every lower finding dispositioned.
  - Phase B, hands-on: a `v0.26.1` store, with its placeholder rows, opens and reads under the tag. Upgrade, rollback and
    re-upgrade pass 9 of 9 steps on three stores. On both supported host builds at the tag the regression suite passes
    6,291 of 6,292 tests. The one failure is a test-isolation defect in a benchmark-instrument test; it fails the same
    way at `v0.26.1` and is fixed on `main` (#1041).
  - Phase C: 2 cells, 44 turns each with 0 timeouts, a restart and a re-paste. They committed
    28 (13 + 15) compactions with no loss and no conflict. The slowest compaction took 68.0 s (bar: 145 s).
    No probe was LOST.
- **Defects:** no respin-bar defect that managed profiles can reach is open.
- **Recall scorecard, fast tier (#898): PASS.** 0 per-question `lcm_recall` flips and
  0 full-text flips against `v0.26.1` over 500 questions; recall@10 is 0.8473, unchanged from `v0.26.1`.

This patch rides a minor that already passed its 24-hour reference-agent window. That window is a per-minor gate, so
none runs for this patch.

Patch release on top of `v0.26.1` (`5fc3d1c6`), cut from `release/v0.26.x`. Theme: what a person pastes, the agent
reads.
- **Before:** with large-output externalization on, a user or assistant message longer than the externalization
  threshold (12,000 characters in the reference agent's configuration) was stored as a one-line stub with no preview
  and no read hint. For a user message the stub also replaced the paste in what the model received, from the turn the
  paste arrived onward, so the agent never saw it and was not told how to open it. Assistant text stayed in the live conversation, but
  for both roles the stored message and its full-text index contained only the stub. Default history search and
  recall's full-text arm could not match words present only in the payload; explicit current-session `lcm_grep`
  searches with `content_scope="externalized"` or `"both"` could still find them within the payload scan limits.
- **After:** user, assistant and other non-tool text is externalized only when it is over 100,000 characters or at
  least 25,000 tokens as the plugin counts them; below both it is stored and replayed as written. Without tiktoken
  the count is an estimate (`len // 4 + 1` for ASCII, so 25,000 at 99,996 characters); dense scripts such as CJK reach
  it sooner. When externalized, the stub carries a short preview of the start and end of the text and a read hint
  (`read it with lcm_expand`), so the agent can open the full text on demand.
- **Unchanged:** tool output and media follow the existing externalization rules and threshold. No config key was
  added, removed or renamed; the existing externalization keys keep their meaning for tool output.
- **Already-stored stubs:** rows that an earlier version already replaced with a stub are not rewritten. Each one is
  still readable with `lcm_expand`.
- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged.
- No new setting, no schema change (schema 5) and no new table. The only prompt change is one system-note clause
  naming user/assistant payload stubs as readable with `lcm_expand`.
- This release never moves a deployed pin by itself. A deployment moves only when its operator re-pins it.

## Changes since v0.26.1

- **#1016 (#1020, #1031): user, assistant and other non-tool text is externalized only above 100,000 characters or at
  25,000 tokens or more as the plugin counts them.**
  - Below both bounds, that text is never externalized, whatever the configured threshold.
  - When externalized, the stub keeps the `ref=` field last (so earlier readers still parse it) and adds a preview
    and the read hint.
  - The preview passes through the plugin's existing sensitive-text patterns (best effort; #1034). It writes
    `quarantined_assistant_output` as `quarantined-assistant-output`, so the stub never breaks replay identity: the
    rc1 sweep's P0, fixed in rc2 (#1031).
  - Tool output, media and the externalization settings are unchanged.
- **Tests (#1020, #1031):** 23 new tests in `tests/test_issue_1016_nontool_externalization_floor.py`. They cover:
    - the floor in characters and in tokens (CJK);
    - the preview's bounds and determinism;
    - ref forging;
    - redaction of the preview, including a label or PEM `BEGIN` line just outside the tail window;
    - the quarantine token on cold replay;
    - the `v0.26.1` recognizer reading the new stub after a rollback.

    Existing externalization tests were adapted to the floor.
- **Docs:** this patch's identity.

## Qualification

- **Adversarial sweep.** Six finders across two model families covered:
  - correctness, security and privacy, performance and DoS, and upgrade, rollback and migration (one family);
  - the contract with readers and the host, and concurrency (the other family).

  They found no P0, P1 or P2. Two P3 findings were dispositioned:
  - **Token estimate on hosts without tiktoken.** There, dense ASCII text under 100,000 characters stays inline above
    25,000 real tokens. This is the documented behaviour, and it matters only below a ~120k-token model window. Noted on #1029.
  - **System-note text check.** A whole-text comparison of the system note cannot match a system row that sits in the
    conversation messages. Hermes does not keep one there. Noted on #998.
- **Full suite** at this tree, run the CI way: 6,248 passed, 92 skipped, 16 xfailed,
  0 failed.
- **Gauntlet at the `v0.26.2-rc2` tag** (receipts are attached to this release):
  - [`PHASE-A-RECEIPT.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/PHASE-A-RECEIPT.md): the all-tools matrix on a fresh clone across privacy postures, plus
    the planted-secret, opt-out, durable-redaction and misconfiguration batteries. All pass, identical to
    `v0.26.1-rc1`.
  - [`PHASE-B-SEAM-RECEIPT.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/PHASE-B-SEAM-RECEIPT.md): the seam check on a pinned live host with the
    reference agent's externalization settings. A short paste is stored and replayed as full text and is found by
    full-text search; a long paste is a stub with a preview and a read hint; tool output matches `v0.26.1`. Counts
    and verdicts only.
  - [`PHASE-B-RECEIPT.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/PHASE-B-RECEIPT.md): the release manager's Phase B verdict over the sweep and the
    hands-on lane.
  - [`PHASE-B-DISPOSITION.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/PHASE-B-DISPOSITION.md): the adversarial sweep of `v0.26.1..v0.26.2-rc2` and the
    disposition of every finding.
  - [`PHASE-B-HANDSON-RECEIPT.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/PHASE-B-HANDSON-RECEIPT.md): the regression suites on each supported host build
    at the tag, and a `v0.26.1` store opened under the tag.
  - [`PHASE-C-RECEIPT.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/PHASE-C-RECEIPT.md): a live `hermes acp` soak, 44 turns per cell with a restart and a

  - [`SCORECARD-FAST-TIER.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.26.2/SCORECARD-FAST-TIER.md): recall at the tag against `v0.26.1`, question by question.

## Known follow-ups

## Benchmark boundary

- No retrieval or QA benchmark claim. The product change is the non-tool externalization floor, the stub preview and
  one system-note clause.
- The recall scorecard's fast tier (#898: embeddings off, every rc) ran at the rc2 tag against `v0.26.1`, question by
  question: 0 `lcm_recall` flips and 0 full-text flips over 500 questions. The
  embeddings-on rows are per-minor and do not run for this patch.

## Upgrade

- **Install:** plugin only. Verify the exact commit, install this tag at it and restart the gateway. No migration.
- **Rollback:** to `v0.26.1`, plugin only. The store is unchanged (schema 5); text stored in full by this version is
  ordinary text to `v0.26.1`.
- **Settings:** none.
